title: Signal envelope (v1)
description: The canonical, backend-agnostic wire form of a stakeholder Signal in the think-and-ship signals SaaS (Phase 30). This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the Rust core validates against it (serde + a schema test) and the TS edge generates its types from it (json-schema-to-typescript), so the two can never drift. A `SignalEnvelope` is a strict superset of the local `Signal` type (Phase 29a): the local fields are present unchanged, plus the cloud fields (`schema_version`, `tenant_id`, `idempotency_key`, `source`, `attribution`) every adapter must populate. See docs/SIGNAL_CONTRACT.md for the prose contract, the idempotency-key rule, the tenant-identity model, the OAuth 2.1 auth scheme, and the remote-MCP sync surface.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS envelope schema. Bumped only on a breaking envelope change, independently of any backend or local-Signal version. Pin to the integer-as-string form to mirror the dev.thinkandship `schema` convention in docs/SCHEMA.md.

id.description: Stable, globally-unique signal id (UUIDv4 minted by the first writer — the ingest adapter or the local agent). Distinct from `idempotency_key`: `id` identifies the record, `idempotency_key` identifies the upstream event so re-delivery of the same event collapses onto one record.

tenant_id.description: The tenant this signal belongs to. EQUALS the local `resolve_project_id()` value (`<basename>-<6hex(cwd)>` or the THINK_AND_SHIP_PROJECT_NAME override), so the same cwd maps to the same cloud tenant and one tenant = one Durable Object. Cross-tenant reads are never permitted (see docs/SIGNAL_CONTRACT.md §Tenant isolation).

from.description: Human-facing attribution string (display name / handle / email local-part). The authenticated, structured identity lives in `attribution`; `from` is the always-present cheap label, mirroring the local Signal.from field.

body.description: The signal content as submitted (plain text or Markdown). Adapters MUST NOT pre-summarize; enrichment is additive and lives in `enrichment[]`.

created.description: When the signal was first created at its origin (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601, UTC). For adapter-sourced signals this is the upstream event time when known, else the ingest time.

updated.description: Last mutation time (RFC 3339, UTC). Set by the canonical store on every write; absent on a freshly-created signal.

idempotency_key.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 that lets ANY adapter dedupe re-delivery of the same upstream event. Computed identically everywhere (see docs/SIGNAL_CONTRACT.md §Idempotency): sha256(tenant_id \u241f source.adapter \u241f source.external_id) when the adapter has a stable upstream id, else sha256(tenant_id \u241f kind \u241f from \u241f body \u241f created). \u241f (U+241F) is the field separator. The canonical store treats a colliding key as a no-op upsert.

enrichment.description: Append-only enrichment trail produced by the agent churning on the signal (Phase 29d). Ordered oldest-first.

cross_refs.description: Typed cross-references into the think/ship/roadmap graph, in the existing `prefix:value` wire form (infra/cross_ref.rs), extended with the `signal:` variant (Phase 29b). Bidirectional: promoting a signal writes `chunk:<id>` here and `signal:<id>` onto the chunk.

SignalKind.description: What kind of stakeholder input this is. Matches the local Signal vocabulary (Phase 29a).

SignalStatus.description: Lifecycle state. Legal transitions (enforced by the canonical store, mirroring the local engine): new\u2192triaged\u2192researched\u2192surfaced\u2192promoted; any non-terminal state \u2192 dismissed. Backward transitions (e.g. researched\u2192new) are rejected.

Source.description: Which edge adapter produced the signal and the upstream coordinates needed to dedupe it (Phase 30c). `external_id` is the adapter's stable upstream identifier (GitHub issue node id, email Message-ID, webhook delivery id); when present it feeds the idempotency key.

received_at.description: When the edge accepted the inbound event (RFC 3339, UTC).

Attribution.description: Structured, optionally-authenticated identity of the submitter. Distinct from `from` (the cheap display label). `authenticated` is true only when the submitter proved identity via the tenant's auth (OAuth 2.1) rather than an anonymous public-submit path.

subject.description: The OAuth 2.1 access-token subject (`sub`) when the submitter authenticated.

Enrichment.description: One agent enrichment record (Phase 29d): the reasoning step that motivated it, the external sources consulted, a summary, and a confidence. Append-only.

think_step.description: The think_* step number that produced this enrichment (cross-ref into the reasoning trace).

sources.description: External references consulted (URLs, doc ids, ministr symbol ids).

confidence.description: Agent confidence in this enrichment, 0..1. The surfacing gate (Phase 29e) only raises researched signals above a threshold.

at.description: When the enrichment was recorded (RFC 3339, UTC).

CrossRef.description: A cross-reference in the existing wire form `prefix:value`. `prefix` is one of the think/ship/roadmap families plus `signal`. Mirrors infra/cross_ref.rs::CrossRef::from_wire so the same parser accepts it.

examples.body: The roadmap export drops sub-bullets when a chunk has nested acceptance notes.

enrichment.summary: Confirmed: export_markdown renders acceptance[] flat; nested notes are not modeled on Chunk. Maps to the done richer-roadmap-export chunk.
